sasha: heads-up — saw a persistent perf regression on the multi-node pipelined run after the kernel-select changes. end-to-end p50 up ~22% on 13B TP=2 PP=2 runs.
kevin: can you paste the perf snapshot and minimal profile?
sasha: pasted below from perf-bot run (step 120). quick TL;DR: all-reduce and host memcpy are dominating on cross-node steps.
perf-bot: PERF SNAPSHOT: model=13B, tp=2, pp=2, batch=1, seq=2048, tokens_per_sec=42, p50_latency=820ms
perf-bot: PROFILE_SUMMARY:
```
[step 120] compute=68ms; allreduce=42ms; host_memcpy=18ms; idle=5ms
intra-node (nvlink) allreduce ~6ms
cross-node (efa) allreduce ~46ms
```
maria: the new kernel selector started preferring an 'optimized' fused kernel on-device but falls back to a host-copy path when chunk sizes exceed the PCIe threshold. that fallback causes extra memcpy and triggers EFA collectives for shards.
ryan: that matches what i've seen — cross-node collects suffer when we have many small tensors. NCCL's startup overhead + driver per-message cost on EFA is large for tiny messages.
kevin: two orthogonal mitigations: 1) coalesce small grads before all-reduce (runtime-level aggregator), 2) tweak kernel selection so cross-node fallback happens at larger chunk sizes only when beneficial.
sasha: tried enabling NCCL async and overlapping with compute, but stalls remain because KV cache flush points force a sync all-reduce. KV cache behavior is exposing additional barriers.
maria: can you share the lightweight profile that shows ordering?
sasha: pasted short timeline (condensed):
```
[t=0] compute forward stream A
[t=68ms] backward compute ends, schedule allreduce stream B
[t=70ms] host memcpy started (18ms)
[t=88ms] allreduce (efa) runs 46ms blocking completion before next compute slice
```
ryan: looks like memcpy + start latency pushes the allreduce into the critical path. for PP=2 we have narrow windows to overlap. aggregated messages would help.
kevin: propose a runtime flag to try: `comm_coalesce_ms` + `comm_chunk_max_bytes` and a conservative `kernel_select.cross_node_pref` option. quick canary command: 
```
./run_infra_test --model=13B --tp=2 --pp=2 --batch=1 --seq=2048 \
  --kernel-hint=prefer-intra-node --comm-chunk=64KB --comm_coalesce_ms=3 --enable-nccl-async=true
```
sasha: running the canary now on 3-node cluster (2 GPUs/node). will post numbers.
kevin: also add a micro-batcher that accumulates grads up to 64KB or 3ms then emits a single reduce. avoids lots of tiny NCCl ops.
maria: note: EFA shows measurable per-message overhead under ~1KB. anything smaller should be aggregated. also check driver stats with `ibv_devinfo` and our RDMA counters.
ryan: we should also adjust kernel selector to prefer device kernels for intra-node and only use host-fallback when we detect true PCIe saturation (comm_bandwidth_usage > threshold). avoids unnecessary host copies for cross-node-friendly tensors.
sasha: canary results: allreduce collapsed from 42ms -> 12ms after coalesce and comm-chunk tweaks. end-to-end p50 down ~15%. observed one node still had occasional IPC spikes during backward (node1), need follow-up.
kevin: nice. next steps: 1) add comm_coalesce_ms config with sane default (2-5ms) 2) add a kernel-select gate for cross-node host-fallback tied to comm saturation metric 3) implement per-shard KV prefetch to minimize sync points.
maria: i'll prototype a kernel-select param patch and add unit test for chunk boundary behavior.
ryan: i'll open a small perf harness to measure EFA per-message latency and help set defaults for `comm_chunk` and `comm_coalesce_ms`.
sasha: opening PR with the runtime config + a canary script. tag reviewers @kevin @maria. :thumbsup:
kevin: review when available. also add a short README for ops: how to tune coalesce/chunk for different fabrics (nvlink vs pcie vs efa). :memo:
perf-bot: NOTE: experiment id=exp-1987, results attached to perf dashboard (link)
sasha: thanks everyone — will follow up with a postmortem if the node spikes persist. :eyes:
